The verb that the ULT translates as **you looked** could be third-person feminine singular or second-person masculine singular. Those two forms coincide in the case of this verb. If it is feminine singular, then it is a personification of the city of Jerusalem as a woman, as in verses 1–3 and 7. If it is the masculine singular form of “you,” it would be addressing a representative Israelite. If a translation of the Bible exists in your region, you may wish to use the reading that it uses. If a translation of the Bible does not exist in your region, you may wish to use the reading of the ULT. If you do, use the singular form of “you” in your translation if your language marks that distinction, and use the feminine form if your language marks that distinction. Alternate translation: [and he looked] or [and one looked]
